title: Bangkok Midnight Marathon 2026 Review: Crossing a Cable-Stayed Bridge After Dark
seo_title: Bangkok Midnight Marathon 2026 Review | Rama VIII Bridge
meta_description: Bangkok Midnight Marathon 2026 review: December 20 near the Rama VIII Bridge and Sanam Luang -- a nighttime race on a landmark Chao Phraya crossing.
dek: Set for 20 December 2026 near Rama VIII Bridge and Sanam Luang, this nighttime race runs on and around one of Bangkok's most recognisable modern landmarks -- a 475-metre cable-stayed bridge over the Chao Phraya River.
verdict: The Bangkok Midnight Marathon puts runners near a genuine architectural landmark: the Rama VIII Bridge, an asymmetrical cable-stayed bridge with a striking inverted-Y pylon, opened in 2002 and named for King Ananda Mahidol. Its nighttime format echoes the HOKA Midnight Run and VnExpress Midnight races covered elsewhere in this research batch, though organised independently by Taozing Running Club. Two distances (21.098K/10K) with genuinely wide aggregator coverage -- five distinct listings -- suggest solid local visibility despite registration status not yet being confirmed.

sections.heading: Racing Near an Architectural Landmark
paragraphs: The Bangkok Midnight Marathon offers two distances -- 21.098K and 10K -- around the Rama VIII Bridge and Sanam Luang area, organised by Taozing Running Club. [1] The Rama VIII Bridge is a cable-stayed bridge crossing the Chao Phraya River, built between 1999-2002 to relieve traffic on the nearby Phra Pinklao Bridge, opened on 7 May 2002 and named for King Ananda Mahidol (Rama VIII). [2]

sections.heading: A Distinctive Asymmetrical Design
paragraphs: The bridge features an asymmetrical design with a single inverted-Y pylon on the west bank, 84 cables, a total length of 475 metres, a height of 160 metres, and a longest span of 300 metres. [2] It connects Phra Nakhon and Bang Phlat Districts, near landmarks including the Bangkok National Museum and the historic Sanam Luang ceremonial ground -- giving this course genuine architectural and cultural significance.

sections.heading: A Third Midnight-Branded Race
paragraphs: This joins the HOKA Midnight Run Asia series and the VnExpress Marathon Hanoi Midnight covered elsewhere in this research batch as a third distinctly nighttime-branded race -- though organised independently by Taozing Running Club rather than either of those series. [1] The pattern suggests nighttime racing is a genuinely growing format across Southeast Asia, not an isolated experiment.

sections.heading: Wide but Fragmented Visibility
paragraphs: Research turned up five distinct aggregator listings for this race -- AIMS World Running, Ahotu, World's Marathons, AllEvents, and PaceBuilder -- but no single dominant official site emerged. [1] That breadth of secondary coverage, without a clearly primary source, suggests the race has real local visibility even if its direct online presence is less centralised than some other events.

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: If crossing a genuinely striking piece of modern Bangkok architecture at night appeals, the Bangkok Midnight Marathon on 20 December 2026 is a distinctive pick with real aggregator visibility. Registration status wasn't confirmed at the time of this research, so check multiple listing sites for the latest sign-up details.

faqs.question: What is the Rama VIII Bridge?
faqs.answer: A cable-stayed bridge crossing Bangkok's Chao Phraya River, built 1999-2002 and named for King Ananda Mahidol (Rama VIII). It has a striking asymmetrical design with a single inverted-Y pylon and 84 cables. The race runs near this bridge and Sanam Luang. [2]

faqs.question: Who organises the Bangkok Midnight Marathon?
faqs.answer: Taozing Running Club, organising independently from the HOKA Midnight Run and VnExpress Midnight races covered elsewhere in this research -- part of a broader trend of nighttime race formats growing across Southeast Asia. [1]
